name: Marcus Aurelius Olympius Nemesianus
bio: Marcus Aurelius Olympius Nemesianus was a Latin poet of Carthage who wrote in the later third century AD. He is known mainly for the Cynegetica, an unfinished didactic poem on hunting with dogs and horses, which looks forward to the reign of the emperors Carinus and Numerian, so that he is generally dated to about 283. Ancient notices credit him also with poems on fishing and on seafaring that have not survived.

Four pastoral poems in the manner of Virgil's Eclogues are now commonly given to him. In many manuscripts and older editions they stand after the eclogues of Calpurnius Siculus, and some editors, Keene among them, printed them as Calpurnius's eighth to eleventh. They treat the death of Meliboeus, the love of two boys for a girl shut in her house, Pan's song of the birth of Bacchus, and the sorrows of two shepherds in love.
